VR-RULE-GET-STATE.name: Actions that change state should be restricted to POST
VR-RULE-GET-STATE.why: An MVC action without an HTTP verb attribute accepts GET as well as POST. When such an action changes data or session state, it can be triggered by a link, an image tag or a redirect, and its parameters end up in browser history, proxy logs and Referer headers. Pentesters report this as 'POST to GET method conversion' or 'privilege escalation on GET request'.
VR-RULE-GET-STATE.fix: Add [HttpPost] (and [ValidateAntiForgeryToken]) to every action that creates, updates or deletes data, changes a preference or touches the session. Keep GET for pure reads.
refs: CWE-650: Trusting HTTP permission methods on the server side
OWASP Cheat Sheet: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention

VR-RULE-CSRF.name: POST actions should validate an anti-forgery token
VR-RULE-CSRF.why: Without an anti-forgery token, another website can submit a form to this action using the victim's authenticated session (cross-site request forgery). On login, password reset and password change actions this can log a user into an attacker's account, trigger reset e-mails or change the password. The rule is a hotspot because a global filter (for example AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken) can provide the same protection; confirm before treating it as a vulnerability.
VR-RULE-CSRF.fix: Add [ValidateAntiForgeryToken] to the action and @Html.AntiForgeryToken() to the form, or register a global anti-forgery filter for all unsafe HTTP methods. Do not rely on the presence of a Referer header.
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: Cross-Site Request Forgery Prevention

VR-RULE-PRELOGIN-LOOKUP.name: Pre-login actions should not reveal whether an account exists
VR-RULE-PRELOGIN-LOOKUP.why: Actions on the login page run before authentication. If they take a login name and return different data (business units, culture, flags, connection keys) for existing and unknown accounts, an attacker can enumerate valid user names and then target them with password guessing or phishing. Without throttling, the action becomes an unlimited oracle.
VR-RULE-PRELOGIN-LOOKUP.fix: Return the same response shape and message for known and unknown login names, move these calls behind [HttpPost] with rate limiting, and require authentication for anything that is not needed to render the login form (for example connection keys for security administrators).
compliant: // Same shape for every login name; empty list when unknown
refs: CWE-306: Missing authentication for critical function

VR-RULE-RESET-ENUM.name: Password reset should answer the same way for every account
VR-RULE-RESET-ENUM.why: When the forgot-password flow returns a special message only for accounts that exist (for example 'a reset link was already shared'), anyone can learn which user names are valid. This is the 'password reset discloses whether an account exists' finding reported by pentesters.
VR-RULE-RESET-ENUM.fix: Always show one neutral message such as 'If the details match an account, a reset link has been sent.' Handle the pending-link case silently on the server side.
compliant: return NeutralResetResponse(); // same message and timing as every other request

VR-RULE-COOKIE-AUTHCTX.name: Authentication decisions should not trust data read from a cookie
VR-RULE-COOKIE-AUTHCTX.why: Cookies are fully controlled by the client. If an authentication context (user name, 'authentication successful' flag) is deserialised from a cookie and then used to skip the password check, anyone who can forge that cookie can log in as any user. This is only safe when the cookie is encrypted and integrity-protected with a server-side key. Deserialising client data is also listed in the CWE Top 25 (CWE-502).
VR-RULE-COOKIE-AUTHCTX.fix: Keep the external-login result in server-side session state or in a short-lived, signed and encrypted ticket (for example ASP.NET Data Protection). Verify the signature before deserialising, and never let a client-supplied flag decide whether a password is checked.
compliant: var json = protector.Unprotect(cookieValue);   // throws if tampered
refs: CWE-565: Reliance on cookies without validation and integrity checking

VR-RULE-CUSTOMERRORS-OFF.name: Detailed error pages should not be shown to remote users
VR-RULE-CUSTOMERRORS-OFF.why: With customErrors mode="Off", any unhandled exception returns the ASP.NET 'yellow screen' with the stack trace, source file paths, framework and assembly versions. Attackers use this to map the application and target known weaknesses. Pentest reports call this 'server-side details revealed' or 'verbose error messages'.
VR-RULE-CUSTOMERRORS-OFF.fix: Ship customErrors mode="RemoteOnly" (or "On") with a generic error page, log the exception server-side, and only relax it in development transforms.
refs: CWE-209: Generation of error message containing sensitive information

VR-RULE-DEBUG-TRUE.name: Debug compilation should be disabled in shipped configuration
VR-RULE-DEBUG-TRUE.why: compilation debug="true" disables batch compilation and script optimisation, keeps debug symbols, extends request timeouts and makes error output more detailed. In production it increases information disclosure and resource use.
VR-RULE-DEBUG-TRUE.fix: Set debug="false" in the shipped Web.config and enable it only through a development transform.
refs: CWE-11: ASP.NET misconfiguration: creating debug binary

VR-RULE-ELMAH-REMOTE.name: Error log viewers should not be reachable remotely
VR-RULE-ELMAH-REMOTE.why: ELMAH stores every unhandled error with the full HTTP context: cookies, form fields, server variables and query strings. With allowRemoteAccess enabled and no authorisation rule on elmah.axd, anyone who reaches the site can read session cookies and submitted data, which can lead to session hijacking and credential exposure.
VR-RULE-ELMAH-REMOTE.fix: Set allowRemoteAccess="0", add a <location path="elmah.axd"> rule that allows only administrators, or remove the elmah.axd handler from production builds.
refs: CWE-215: Insertion of sensitive information into debugging code

VR-RULE-NO-HSTS.name: Strict-Transport-Security should be sent on HTTPS responses
VR-RULE-NO-HSTS.why: Without HSTS, a user's first request (or a typed http:// URL) can be intercepted and downgraded to plain HTTP, exposing session cookies and credentials to anyone on the network path (SSL stripping).
VR-RULE-NO-HSTS.fix: Send Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains on every HTTPS response. Emit it from code or the base config so each deployment gets it without manual edits.
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: HTTP Strict Transport Security

VR-RULE-NO-CSP.name: A Content-Security-Policy header should be configured
VR-RULE-NO-CSP.why: A Content-Security-Policy limits where scripts, styles and frames may load from. Without it, any HTML or script injection runs with full privileges and the page can be framed by other sites. This is a hotspot because the header may be added in code rather than in Web.config.
VR-RULE-NO-CSP.fix: Send a CSP from the response pipeline (or customHeaders) that allows only your own origins and required third parties, and add frame-ancestors 'self'. Start with Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only to find violations before enforcing.
refs: CWE-1021: Improper restriction of rendered UI layers
OWASP Cheat Sheet: Content Security Policy

VR-RULE-COOKIE-SECURE.name: Cookies should be marked Secure
VR-RULE-COOKIE-SECURE.why: A cookie without the Secure attribute is also sent over plain HTTP. If any request is made over HTTP (mixed content, a typed URL, a downgrade), the session cookie travels unencrypted and can be captured. Missing SameSite also leaves cookies open to cross-site use.
VR-RULE-COOKIE-SECURE.fix: Set requireSSL="true" and sameSite="Lax" (or "Strict") on httpCookies, and set the same on the session and authentication cookies.
refs: CWE-614: Sensitive cookie in HTTPS session without 'Secure' attribute

VR-RULE-PLAINTEXT-PASSWORD.name: Credentials should not be stored in plain text in configuration
VR-RULE-PLAINTEXT-PASSWORD.why: A password written into a committed config file is visible to everyone with repository or server access, ends up in backups and deployment packages, and is hard to rotate. Pentesters report this as 'sensitive data exposure' or 'password in clear text'.
VR-RULE-PLAINTEXT-PASSWORD.fix: Load the secret from Azure Key Vault (the AzureKeyVault config builder is already declared) or environment variables, rotate it if it was ever real, and keep only a placeholder in source control.

VR-RULE-SESSION-TIMEOUT.name: Session idle timeout should be short
VR-RULE-SESSION-TIMEOUT.why: A long idle timeout keeps an unattended or stolen session usable for hours. Pentesters report this as 'insufficient session expiration'.
VR-RULE-SESSION-TIMEOUT.fix: Use an idle timeout of 15 to 30 minutes for the portal (shorter for administrators) and an absolute session lifetime. Document any business exception.

VR-RULE-REQUEST-LIMIT.name: Request size limits should match real upload needs
VR-RULE-REQUEST-LIMIT.why: Allowing requests of several gigabytes lets a single client tie up bandwidth, disk and memory, and makes unrestricted file upload easier to abuse.
VR-RULE-REQUEST-LIMIT.fix: Set maxAllowedContentLength and maxRequestLength to the largest file the business needs, and enforce stricter limits per upload endpoint.
refs: CWE-770: Allocation of resources without limits

VR-RULE-HTTP-ENDPOINT.name: Service endpoints should use HTTPS
VR-RULE-HTTP-ENDPOINT.why: Calls to http:// endpoints send requests and responses (tax data, pricing, report credentials) without encryption, so anyone on the network path can read or change them. Internal host names and IP addresses in a shipped config also disclose infrastructure details.
VR-RULE-HTTP-ENDPOINT.fix: Use https:// endpoints with transport security, and supply environment-specific addresses through config transforms or App Configuration instead of the base file.
refs: CWE-319: Cleartext transmission of sensitive information
OWASP Cheat Sheet: Transport Layer Security

VR-RULE-SQL-CONCAT.name: SQL queries should not be built by string concatenation
VR-RULE-SQL-CONCAT.why: Concatenating request values into SQL lets an attacker change the query: read other tenants' data, bypass filters or modify records. SQL injection is CWE Top 25 #3.
VR-RULE-SQL-CONCAT.fix: Use parameterised commands or the repository query API; never concatenate input into SQL text. Validate identifiers (column or table names) against an allow-list.
noncompliant: var sql = "SELECT * FROM Contracts WHERE Number = '" + number + "'";
compliant: var cmd = new SqlCommand("SELECT * FROM Contracts WHERE Number = @n", conn);
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: SQL Injection Prevention

VR-RULE-HTML-RAW.name: Html.Raw should not output user-controlled data
VR-RULE-HTML-RAW.why: Html.Raw switches off Razor's automatic HTML encoding. If the value can contain user input (comments, notes, names), injected script runs in other users' browsers (cross-site scripting, CWE Top 25 #1).
VR-RULE-HTML-RAW.fix: Use @value so Razor encodes it. If rich text is required, sanitise it with an allow-list HTML sanitiser before output.
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: Cross Site Scripting Prevention

VR-RULE-OPEN-REDIRECT.name: Redirect targets from the request should be validated
VR-RULE-OPEN-REDIRECT.why: Redirecting to a URL taken from the request lets an attacker send users from a trusted Odessa link to a phishing site.
VR-RULE-OPEN-REDIRECT.fix: Redirect only when Url.IsLocalUrl(returnUrl) is true, or map the value to an allow-list of destinations.
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: Unvalidated Redirects and Forwards

VR-RULE-PATH-TRAVERSAL.name: File paths should not be built from request input
VR-RULE-PATH-TRAVERSAL.why: A file name such as ..\..\Web.config combined into a path lets an attacker read or overwrite files outside the intended folder (path traversal, CWE Top 25 #5).
VR-RULE-PATH-TRAVERSAL.fix: Use Path.GetFileName on the input, combine with a fixed base folder, resolve the full path and check that it still starts with the base folder. Prefer storage IDs over file names.

VR-RULE-SSRF.name: Outbound requests should not use request-supplied URLs
VR-RULE-SSRF.why: If the server fetches a URL supplied by the user, an attacker can make it call internal systems (databases, metadata services, admin APIs) that are not reachable from outside (server-side request forgery, CWE Top 25 #19).
VR-RULE-SSRF.fix: Allow only known hosts and schemes, resolve and block private address ranges, and never pass raw user input to HttpClient or WebClient.

VR-RULE-UNSAFE-DESERIALIZE.name: Deserialisation should not allow arbitrary types
VR-RULE-UNSAFE-DESERIALIZE.why: BinaryFormatter, NetDataContractSerializer, LosFormatter and Json.NET with TypeNameHandling other than None can instantiate attacker-chosen types while deserialising, which leads to remote code execution (CWE Top 25 #16).
VR-RULE-UNSAFE-DESERIALIZE.fix: Use TypeNameHandling.None or a strict SerializationBinder allow-list, and replace BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json or DataContractSerializer with known types.
noncompliant: var settings = new JsonSerializerSettings { TypeNameHandling = TypeNameHandling.All };
compliant: var settings = new JsonSerializerSettings { TypeNameHandling = TypeNameHandling.None };

VR-RULE-PROCESS-START.name: Processes should not be started with variable arguments
VR-RULE-PROCESS-START.why: Passing request data to Process.Start lets an attacker run other commands or add arguments on the server (OS command injection, CWE Top 25 #7).
VR-RULE-PROCESS-START.fix: Avoid starting processes from web requests. If required, use a fixed executable path and pass validated arguments through ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList.
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: OS Command Injection Defense

VR-RULE-WEAK-CRYPTO.name: Weak hashes, ciphers and TLS versions should not be used
VR-RULE-WEAK-CRYPTO.why: MD5, SHA-1, DES, 3DES and RC2 are broken or too weak for security use, and forcing SSL 3.0 or TLS 1.0/1.1 allows downgrade attacks. The Odessa CLAUDE.md also requires SecurityProtocolType.SystemDefault.
VR-RULE-WEAK-CRYPTO.fix: Use SHA-256 or stronger, AES-GCM for encryption, a password hashing function (PBKDF2, bcrypt, Argon2) for passwords, and leave TLS selection to the operating system (SystemDefault).
refs: CWE-327: Use of a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm

VR-RULE-CERT-BYPASS.name: TLS certificate validation should not be disabled
VR-RULE-CERT-BYPASS.why: A certificate validation callback that always returns true accepts any certificate, so a man-in-the-middle can read and alter all traffic to that service.
VR-RULE-CERT-BYPASS.fix: Remove the callback. For private certificate authorities, trust the CA in the machine store or validate the specific certificate thumbprint.
compliant: // No callback: the default validation applies

VR-RULE-HARDCODED-SECRET.name: Secrets should not be hard-coded in source
VR-RULE-HARDCODED-SECRET.why: A password, API key or client secret in source code is shared with everyone who can read the repository and its history, and cannot be rotated without a release.
VR-RULE-HARDCODED-SECRET.fix: Read secrets from Key Vault or environment configuration at runtime and remove them from source and history.
compliant: var apiKey = configuration["Integrations:ApiKey"]; // from Key Vault

VR-RULE-ALLOW-ANONYMOUS.name: Anonymous access should be limited to login and public pages
VR-RULE-ALLOW-ANONYMOUS.why: [AllowAnonymous] removes authentication from an action. On anything other than login, password reset or public content, it exposes business functions or data without a session (missing authentication, CWE Top 25 #25).
VR-RULE-ALLOW-ANONYMOUS.fix: Remove [AllowAnonymous] unless the action must work before login, and add explicit authorisation checks on the rest.
refs: CWE-306: Missing authentication for critical function

VR-DEP.name: Components should not have known published vulnerabilities
VR-DEP.why: A library version that falls inside an advisory's affected range carries a publicly documented weakness. Attackers and vendor scanners fingerprint library versions, so these are among the first issues found in a VAPT ('outdated library', 'vulnerable component'). Severity on this dashboard starts from the advisory's CVSS and is adjusted for how the library is used (shipped to browsers or build-time only).
VR-DEP.fix: Upgrade to the first patched version listed in the advisory, re-run the build and tests, and re-run VulnRadar to confirm. If an upgrade is not possible, document the mitigation and how the vulnerable function is not reachable.
refs: OWASP Top 10:2025 A03 Software Supply Chain Failures
OWASP Cheat Sheet: Vulnerable Dependency Management

VR-RULE-REQUEST-SQL.name: SQL text and connection strings should never come from the request
VR-RULE-REQUEST-SQL.why: An action that accepts SQL text or a connection string as a parameter lets the caller run their own queries against the database, or point the server at any database host it can reach. Even when the SQL is only used to read column metadata, many providers execute the batch, and a supplied connection string can be used to probe internal servers (SQL injection, CWE Top 25 #3, and server-side request forgery, #19).
VR-RULE-REQUEST-SQL.fix: Remove the endpoint from production builds. If it is needed for test tooling, accept only a named query or connection key from an allow-list, never raw SQL or a raw connection string, and require an administrator role.
noncompliant: public ActionResult GetExecutedCommandResult(string sqlCommand, string connectionString = null)
compliant: var sql = AllowedQueries.Get(queryKey);           // fixed, reviewed SQL
refs: OWASP Cheat Sheet: SQL Injection Prevention

VR-RULE-SECRET-DISCLOSURE.name: Connection strings and secrets should not be returned in responses
VR-RULE-SECRET-DISCLOSURE.why: A connection string usually contains the database server, database name and, with SQL authentication, a user name and password. Returning it in JSON hands those details to any caller, browser extension or proxy log, and gives an attacker a direct path to the database.
VR-RULE-SECRET-DISCLOSURE.fix: Do not return connection strings. Return only a display name or a yes/no 'connected' result, and keep credentials in Key Vault. Return a generic failure message instead of the exception text.

VR-RULE-EXCEPTION-MESSAGE.name: Exception messages should not be shown to users
VR-RULE-EXCEPTION-MESSAGE.why: Exception messages often contain SQL errors, server names, file paths, connection details or internal type names. Sending them to the browser helps an attacker map the system; pentesters report it as improper error handling or verbose error messages.
VR-RULE-EXCEPTION-MESSAGE.fix: Log the full exception server-side with a correlation ID and show the user a generic message that includes only that ID.
compliant: return MakeJsonResult(new { error = "The operation failed", reference = id });
refs: CWE-209: Error message containing sensitive information

VR-RULE-TEST-ENDPOINT.name: Test automation endpoints should not ship enabled in production
VR-RULE-TEST-ENDPOINT.why: Test tooling endpoints are built for convenience: they switch to the system user, list all users and business units, run scenarios, delete runs and touch the file system. If they are reachable in a production portal, their protection rests on a single filter and a configuration flag; a weakness in either exposes administrative functions and personal data (active debug code, CWE-489; missing authentication for critical function, CWE-306).
VR-RULE-TEST-ENDPOINT.fix: Exclude the controller from production builds or routes, or require an authenticated administrator plus the test-automation token, and make the security flag impossible to turn off outside test environments. Log every call.
refs: CWE-306: Missing authentication for critical function

VR-RULE-OTP-BRUTEFORCE.name: OTP verification attempts should be limited
VR-RULE-OTP-BRUTEFORCE.why: A six-digit code has one million values. Without a per-user limit on failed verifications, an attacker who has the password can try codes until one works. An in-memory, per-process rate limiter is reset when the application restarts and is not shared between web servers, so it does not give a reliable limit.
VR-RULE-OTP-BRUTEFORCE.fix: Count failed OTP verifications per user in persistent storage, lock or slow down after a small number (e.g. 5), invalidate the code after use or expiry, and apply the limit to every factor type, not only e-mail.
refs: CWE-307: Improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts

VR-RULE-SECURITY-EVENT-LOG.name: Security events should be written to the audit log
VR-RULE-SECURITY-EVENT-LOG.why: Rate-limit hits, failed OTPs and lockouts are the signals a security team needs to spot attacks. System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine is compiled out of release builds, so these events are never recorded in production (security logging and alerting failure, OWASP A09).
VR-RULE-SECURITY-EVENT-LOG.fix: Write the event through the application logger or audit log at warning level with user ID, IP and event type, and make sure it reaches the central log or SIEM.
compliant: DefaultLogger.Instance.LogWarning($"OTP rate limit exceeded", new { type, userId, clientIp });

VR-RULE-OTP-DESTINATION.name: One-time codes should only be sent to the registered destination
VR-RULE-OTP-DESTINATION.why: If the e-mail address or phone number that receives the code comes from data the client can influence, an attacker who knows the password can have the code sent to themselves and bypass MFA. This is the MFA e-mail tampering class the organisation has fixed before.
VR-RULE-OTP-DESTINATION.fix: Read the destination from the stored user record at send time, ignore any value from the model or request, and log a security event when they differ.
compliant: Destination = user.MultiFactorAuthentication.Email,   // from the database, not the model
refs: CWE-639: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key

VR-RULE-OPEN-PROXY.name: Proxies should forward only allow-listed backend endpoints
VR-RULE-OPEN-PROXY.why: A proxy action that appends any request path and query string to a backend URL lets a signed-in user reach every endpoint on that backend with the server's own trust: its network position, the cross-site session and any login token the proxy adds. A substring check to decide when to add a login token can be satisfied by unrelated paths. This is the 'authorization flow bypass via direct backend request' class.
VR-RULE-OPEN-PROXY.fix: Map allowed proxy routes explicitly (controller and action allow-list), reject paths with '..' or encoded separators, add the login token only for the exact login route, and require POST plus anti-forgery validation for forwarded form posts.
compliant: if (!AllowedRoutes.TryGetValue(path, out var route)) return new HttpStatusCodeResult(404);

VR-RULE-PUBLIC-NONACTION.name: Public helpers on base controllers should not be exposed as actions
VR-RULE-PUBLIC-NONACTION.why: In ASP.NET MVC every public, non-static, non-generic method of a controller is an action that can be called by URL, unless it is marked [NonAction]. A public helper on a base controller is therefore reachable on every derived controller (for example /Login/GetApmCompatibleUrl?url=...). Helpers that echo input back can reflect attacker content, and helpers that change state (Close, release locks) can be triggered by any link without the checks the real actions have (exposed dangerous method, CWE-749).
VR-RULE-PUBLIC-NONACTION.fix: Mark helper methods [NonAction], or make them protected or internal. Keep only the intended actions public on base controllers, and give those an explicit HTTP verb attribute.
noncompliant: public string GetApmCompatibleUrl(string url) { ... }   // reachable as /AnyController/GetApmCompatibleUrl?url=...
refs: CWE-749: Exposed dangerous method or function

jiraRefs.summary: [PENTEST] AUTH_04 follow-up - GetBusinessUnitInfos pre-login credential check is an unthrottled password oracle

findings.notes: Four actions on the login controller take a login name and answer differently per account, with no authentication, no HTTP verb restriction and no throttling in this controller: GetBusinessUnitInfos returns the business-unit list or the NoBUsAssigned message; GetDefaultCultureInfo returns a culture or NoDefaultCulture; IsShowForgotPasswordLink returns a per-user flag; GetConnectionKeysForSecurityAdmin returns connection keys for any login name. findings.notes: BeforeLogin() deserialises the ExtLoginDetails request cookie into ExternalAuthenticationContext (lines 54-64). jiraRefs.summary: VAPT - Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Customer Selection Dropdown
SFI | VAPT | Broken Access Control

findings.notes: Close() (line 110) and GetApmCompatibleUrl(string url) (line 132) are public, non-static and not marked [NonAction] on AbstractController, so MVC exposes both as actions on every derived controller. GetApmCompatibleUrl returns its url argument (prefixed with path wildcards when ApmCompatibleUrl is on). On .NET Framework, MVC wraps a string return value in a ContentResult with no content type, so the value is reflected as text/html; request validation normally blocks markup in the query string, which is the only thing standing between this and reflected XSS (the class of PROD01-62682). Close() is overridden in derived controllers (e.g. TwoFactorAuthenticationController line 109); any override that releases locks or changes state can be triggered by URL. Confirm with a GET to /Login/GetApmCompatibleUrl?url=test on a test site, then mark both methods [NonAction] or make them protected.
